audit.why: Early Swain-favoured (ranged W poke, 850-range Nevermove root vs immobile Veigar), late Veigar via uncapped AP — matches page framing.
Spikes covered: Swain 1-3 root chain, 6 Demonic Ascension, mid drain-tank; Veigar Lost Chapter, 6 execute, full build. Content spikes[0..3] all present and grounded.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer level chart says Skill on stages 0-4 while content win[0..4] says Swain — the two layers disagree on 5 rows. breakdown.cooldowns has no digits.
audit.why: Kit supports Swain early: Nevermove 12s CD 850 range roots the immobile Veigar, Q 7s pierce poke, W global-range chip; Veigar's only answer is a 20s E. Content chart is right; full sides moved to agree, whys rewritten to match.
audit.corrected: phases[0..4].side -> Swain with matching whys and 4/10 ratings; real cooldowns (Nevermove 12s, R 120s, E 20s) inserted.

audit.why: Anti-heal vs Ravenous Flock/R drain already named in report[8]; missingInteractions anti-heal rule satisfied.

edits.before: Q through two units on every last-hit — each stack is permanent AP; the lane is a savings account from level 1.
edits.after: Swain's Q bolts out-range you level 1 — take last-hit stacks through two units and concede the trade; stacks win.

edits.before: W on cage-stunned or rooted targets only — uncaged Dark Matter is a donation to his dodge stats.
edits.after: Swain's Nevermove threat rules level 2 — W only on rooted or stunned targets; uncaged Dark Matter whiffs.

edits.before: Cage online: drop it ON yourself when he engages, behind him when he farms — the geometry does the fighting.
edits.after: Cage online but his E-Q chain still wins trades — self-cage when he pulls; the geometry defends, not attacks.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q-stack on cooldown and double-stack off cannon waves. The curve is the matchup.
edits.after: Swain still out-trades — Q-stack on cooldown, double-stack cannon waves, dodge Nevermove; the curve is coming.

edits.before: Primordial Burst online — anyone under half is now a math problem with one answer. Count R damage out loud.
edits.after: His 120s R drain outlasts your one rotation at 6 — Primordial Burst only finishes what cage and W started.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain mode — disengage and reset the fight when it starts. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E Event Horizon (self-cage) has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Demonic Ascension: 120s — his drain mode; disengage when it starts and fight in the window after. - Nevermove is a 12s cooldown at rank 1 — trade in the ten seconds after he misses it. - Your 20s E is the whole defence: self-cage when it all goes wrong, R when it all goes right.

edits.before: Cage his step-up, W the edge-stun, Q-auto, and walk — a half-bar trade that also deposited three stacks into the curve.
edits.after: Drop Event Horizon on his approach path the moment he steps up for Nevermove — the edge stun buys the full W-Q rotation.

edits.before: W-ing open ground on a moving target and trading uncaged 'just to stack' — Veigar without the wall is a piggy bank with a hat.
edits.after: His W poke and Nevermove root make forced contests expensive — let bad waves go and take the stacks the safe waves offer.

edits.before: Swain wins by landing Demonic Ascension, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Swain wins by rooting you with Nevermove, chaining Q bolts into it, and dragging every trade long enough to drain.

notes: Content chart (Swain 0-4, Skill 5, Veigar 6) kept as authority; packet defect flags it against the 54.72% win rate, but the win rate is earned by scaling — Swain winning early stages is kit-grounded (850-range root vs zero mobility) and both layers now agree. Suspect name 'Phenomenal Evil' is Riot's own passive name (full: 'Phenomenal Evil Power') — not a fabrication, left alone. missingInteractions resistances-invalidated (Swain P percent-health flag) not added: Swain P grants HIM max health, it does not bypass Veigar's resistances — flag appears to be a tooltip-parse misfire; recorded here instead of shipping it. sectionsMissing: breakdown.carry, breakdown.feeding, ahead remain owner-generic templates but contain no Swain-specific falsehood and I had no grounded replacement within the length band beyond the fields already edited.
